programme.title: Premier League: Best Goals 2005/06
programme.desc: A look back at the best goals from the 2005/06 season. Thierry Henry became the first player in the league's history to win the Golden Boot four times, top-scoring with 27 goals.

programme.title: Premier League: Best Goals 2006/07
programme.desc: A look back at the best goals from the 2006/07 season. Chelsea's Didier Drogba topped the scoring charts with 20 goals, ahead of Benni McCarthy (18) and Cristiano Ronaldo (17).

programme.title: Premier League: Best Goals 2007/08
programme.desc: A look back at the best goals from the 2007/08 season. Cristiano Ronaldo topped the scoring charts with a remarkable 31 goals, ahead of Fernando Torres and Emmanuel Adebayor on 24.

programme.title: Premier League: Best Goals 2008/09
programme.desc: A look back at the best goals from the 2008/09 season. Chelsea striker Nicolas Anelka secured the Golden Boot with 19 goals, beating Cristiano Ronaldo to the prize.

programme.title: Premier League: Best Goals 2009/10
programme.desc: We revisit the best goals from the 2009/2010 season. In his most prolific season for Chelsea, Didier Drogba secured the Golden Boot with 29 goals, three ahead of Wayne Rooney.

programme.title: Premier League: Best Goals 2011/12
programme.desc: A look back at the best goals from the 2011/12 season. With 30 goals, Robin van Persie won the Golden Boot in his final season for Arsenal, finishing three ahead of Wayne Rooney.

programme.title: Premier League Review: 2012/13
programme.desc: A review of the 2012/13 season. Sir Alex Ferguson ended his managerial career as Manchester United clinched their 13th Premier League title and FA Cup winners Wigan were relegated.

programme.desc: A review of the 2013/14 season. Manchester City clinched their second Premier League title, Jose Mourinho returned to Chelsea and Tony Pulis masterminded a great escape at Palace.

programme.desc: A review of the 2014/15 season. Eden Hazard's superb form helped Chelsea clinch their fifth title, while newly-promoted Burnley and QPR made immediate returns to the Championship.

programme.desc: A review of the 2015/16 season. Leicester City shocked the footballing world, Jose Mourinho's second tenure at Chelsea came to an end and Newcastle dropped into the second tier.

programme.desc: A look back at the best goals from the 2016/17 season. Harry Kane won the Golden Boot for the second successive season with 29 goals, scoring seven goals in Spurs' last two games.
